items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] They're a relief of what might be, Manon. Yeah.

ctx.x: The rock and roll guys do the same thing in their shift up of a half tone for the next chorus. They're trying to do that.

They're a relief of what might be, Manon. Yeah. The question, you bring up something here, the question of the importance of the tune. We have a great affection for the New Orleans repertoire, the Dixieland tunes, and the Dixieland revivalists have a great affection for them, and even the Chicagoans have a great affection for them. Do you think that the tune might also have been important in making jazz a New Orleans derivative? Do you think that, if without Dixieland tunes, that there might have been a Dixieland…

If you analyze the tunes that the Wolverines played, presumably unaffected, you'll find that when they play Royal Garden or Jasmine Blues, those are the weakest things they played. And they played them totally different from New Orleans. When they play a tune like Need Some Padding or Susie, which were written in Chicago, the band plays infinitely better.
